clue.text: Gather a scholar's into dope

indicators.note: into tells you the scholar's letters go inside the word for a dope

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
a scholar is an MA, a Master of Arts; the 's stands for is, saying where the letters go

explanation.surface: Someone collects up a learned person's belongings and stuffs them into a stash of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' reads as drugs or inside information, but here it is a fool, and 'into' sends the scholar's degree inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to collect or accumulate things into a pile is to gather them.

clue.text: Each naval failure adds up to downfall

indicators.note: a failure is a breakdown, so the two words before it break down into a new order

explanation.surface: Every defeat at sea contributes to a nation's eventual collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failure' is the anagram signal for EACH NAVAL, and 'adds up to' merely links to the definition, which is literal: a mass of snow that falls down.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical literal sense: a mass of snow sliding off a mountain is quite literally a fall downwards.

clue.text: Excited atmosphere surrounding a holy man

indicators.note: surrounding says the word for atmosphere goes around the holy man

parts.note: the atmosphere is the air
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A thrilled crowd gathers round a saintly figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts AIR around ST, the abbreviation for saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a place that is up and bustling with agitation is in an excited state.

clue.text: Prompt acknowledgements of indebtedness that appear phoney

parts.note: to prompt someone is to spur them into action
IOUs are written notes admitting a debt, I owe you

explanation.surface: Debt notes that arrive suspiciously quickly turn out to be forgeries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like an adjective meaning quick, but it is the verb meaning to urge on.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something fake or not genuine is phoney.

clue.text: Many have just become clear

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, which crosswords call many
to have something is to own it
what is just is right, fair and proper

explanation.surface: Lots of people have only recently understood something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' reads as an adverb meaning recently, but it is the adjective meaning fair. 'Many' for a large Roman numeral, here D for 500, is an old crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as an adjective: a plain, out-and-out lie is a clear lie.

clue.text: Speed, causing dismay

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to rush or hurry along
as a verb, to discourage or crush someone's hopes

explanation.definitionFit: Two verb senses: to rush somewhere quickly, and to crush someone's hopes and so dishearten them.

clue.text: The president's not up to cleaning for a start

indicators.note: for a start says the cleaning word comes first, ahead of the turned word

parts.note: washing is cleaning with water

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word before it is written from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: The head of state refuses to do the housework, to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NOT into TON, and 'for a start' places WASHING ahead of it. 'not up to' reads as one idiom meaning incapable of, hiding the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: George, the first holder of the American presidency.

clue.text: The City is set in mature way of doing things

indicators.note: is set in says the City's letters are placed inside the word for mature

parts.note: ripe fruit is mature fruit
the City is London's financial district, whose postcode area is EC

explanation.surface: London's financial district is stuck in its grown-up habits.
explanation.walkthrough: The City, capitalised, is London's financial district, which lies in the East Central postal area; 'is set in' places that postcode within the word for mature.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a formula or method for achieving a result, as in cookery.

clue.text: This Prime Minister could make lads get on!

indicators.note: could make says the letters of the name can be rearranged into the three words that follow, and so they into it

explanation.surface: A premier whose policies might help young men advance in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' is the anagram signal, run backwards: the letters of the answer could make LADS GET ON. William Ewart, four times British premier under Queen Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Victorian Liberal leader who headed four British governments.

clue.text: Edward receiving a Greek character, though with little warmth

indicators.note: receiving says Edward's short name takes the Greek letter inside it

parts.note: Ted is a familiar form of Edward
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Edward greets a visitor from Athens, but coolly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet, which 'receiving' places within the man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lukewarm, whether of water or of a welcome.

clue.text: People who don't think much of themselves

definitions.text: People who don't think much of themselves

parts.words: People who don't think much of themselves
parts.note: the phrase suggests low self-esteem, but read literally it describes those who spend little thought on their own interests because they put others first

explanation.definitionFit: Literal reading: selfless folk give little thought to their own interests, putting others first.

clue.text: Applaud about head of school's catch

indicators.note: about says the word for applaud goes around the letter from school

parts.note: to applaud is to clap

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Pupils cheer their headmaster's prize fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts S, from 'head of school's', inside CLAP. The catch is a fastening, not a haul.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: the fastening on a necklace or bag.

clue.text: Alarmed by a feminine incursion

parts.note: F is the grammar abbreviation for feminine
an incursion is a raid into enemy territory

explanation.surface: Men are startled when women burst into their club.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: frightened, feeling fear.

clue.text: The underworld boss struck an attitude when so inclined

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god who ruled the underworld
to strike an attitude is to pose, so struck one is posed

explanation.surface: A gangland chief puts on airs whenever the mood takes him.
explanation.walkthrough: The underworld is the classical land of the dead, ruled by Dis, not a criminal gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: willing or of a mind to do something.

clue.text: Health-centre to impress the woman in general

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letters of the word it is hyphenated to

parts.note: to get someone is to affect or move them, as in that tune really gets me
the woman, as an object pronoun, is her

explanation.surface: A clinic sets out to win over female patients as a whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes AL from the middle of heALth. 'Health-centre' looks like one noun, a clinic, but splits into fodder and instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: on the whole, taken all in all.

clue.text: Conceal nothing — make a glum face about it

indicators.note: about it says the reworked letters go around the letter for nothing
make tells you to form something new out of the three words that follow

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Give nothing away, and pull a miserable expression as you do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' asks for a rearrangement of the three words after it, giving CAMUFLAGE, and 'about it' wraps that around the letter for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to disguise something so it cannot be seen.

clue.text: Smuggled drink only coming out at night

definitions.meaning: a description of the light from the moon, seen only after dark

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: illicit liquor made or run by night, and the lunar glow visible only after dark.

clue.text: Frozen fish out of the lake

indicators.note: out of here means outside of, so the fish goes around the lake

parts.note: a cod is a sea fish
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Icy fish hauled straight from the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' means outside, so COD goes around L. It reads as removal from the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: very chilly, as in I'm frozen.

clue.text: Vending machine at the pharmacy?

definitions.meaning: a machine that gives out goods or drinks
the person in a chemist's shop who makes up and hands out prescriptions

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a machine that hands out goods, and a chemist who makes up prescriptions.

clue.text: Made an opening to extend garden plot outside

indicators.note: outside says the garden plot goes around the word for extend

parts.note: a bed is a plot of garden for flowers
to reach is to extend or stretch out

explanation.surface: A gardener knocked through a gap to enlarge the vegetable patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: broke through a wall or defence, creating a gap.

clue.text: Poetry composd quietly in the dawn

indicators.note: in says the letter for quietly sits inside the name for the dawn

parts.note: Eos is the Greek goddess of the dawn
P is piano, the music marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Verses written softly at daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P inside EOS, the Greek goddess of the dawn. 'composed' simply links.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: epic verse, or a body of it, handed down in a tradition.

clue.text: Dull company. — don't give so many dirty looks

parts.words: don't give so many dirty looks
parts.note: to lour is to scowl, so to scowl less often is to lour less

explanation.surface: Faced with boring guests, try not to glare at them so much.
explanation.walkthrough: To lour (or lower) is to scowl, so giving fewer dirty looks is, whimsically, to LOUR LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lacking vividness or interest, drab.

clue.text: She's written two articles without raising support

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the articles go around the turned support

parts.note: an is an indefinite article
a is the other indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means the word after it is written upwards

parts.note: a leg supports a table or a body

explanation.surface: An author has produced two pieces with no help in fundraising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense meaning outside, not lacking, so the articles go round the support, which 'raising' turns upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a woman's first name, clued simply as a female.

clue.text: Tea's been prepared, but he won't come

indicators.note: prepared says the two words before it have been made up into something new

parts.note: the letters of the word without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: The meal is on the table, yet a guest is going to stay away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' is the anagram signal for TEAS BEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a person who fails to turn up when expected.

clue.text: Expect a temporary delay

parts.note: a wait is a short hold-up before something happens

explanation.surface: Be prepared for a brief hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to look forward to something that is coming.

clue.text: T-junction muddle

parts.note: an angle is where two lines meet, their junction

explanation.surface: Confusion at a three-way road crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T-junction' looks like one road term but splits at the hyphen into a letter and a meeting of lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a confused, knotted mess.

clue.text: Having inside knowledge about a golf-course

indicators.note: having inside says the word for knowledge holds the word for about within it

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone with privileged information on a place to play golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside knowledge' reads as one phrase, but 'Having inside' is the container signal and knowledge alone is the British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose sense: strictly the putting surface, but also an old word for the whole links.

clue.text: Turns over rented accommodation

definitions.meaning: breaks up and turns soil with a spade

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: works soil with a spade, and British slang for lodgings.

clue.text: Lively, though the time is around 1.50

indicators.note: is around says the word for the time goes round the numerals

parts.note: an age is a period of time
in Roman numerals 1 is I and 50 is L

explanation.surface: Still full of energy even though it is nearly two o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 1.50 is not a clock time but two Roman numerals side by side, which 'is around' places within the word for a period.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: nimble, quick in movement.

clue.text: Improves a number among the laying birds

indicators.note: among says the number sits within the word for the birds

parts.note: hens are the birds kept for laying eggs
eight is a number

explanation.surface: A farmer upgrades several of his egg-producing flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: makes greater or more intense, enhances.

clue.text: A ruse thus bungled might well lead to an exchange of words!

definitions.text: might well lead to an exchange of words
definitions.note: a description rather than a synonym: a thing that lets you swap one word for another

indicators.note: bungled means botched, so the three words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A trick that goes wrong like this is likely to start a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungled' is the anagram signal for A RUSE THUS. An exchange of words is not a quarrel but swapping one word for a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: a book of synonyms lets a writer swap one term for another.

clue.text: Foreign currency in hand — in a reserve fund

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: Cash from abroad that is kept ready, set aside for emergencies.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' signals that the answer lies inside 'hanD IN A Reserve'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the money of Serbia, Jordan, Kuwait and other countries.
